summary: This is a Docker Compose configuration that defines a service called 'app'. It builds a Docker image from the current directory, maps port 8000 on the host to port 80 in the container, and mounts a local Python file into the container so changes to main.py are reflected instantly without rebuilding.

explanations.5: The syntax %%port=8000%% is a template variable that gets replaced with 8000; the colon separates the host port (8000) from the container port (80), meaning traffic to localhost:8000 reaches port 80 inside the container.
explanations.7: This mounts the local file ./main.py as a volume at /code/main.py inside the container, so the running app uses the live version of your file instead of a static copy made during the build.
